institution: Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Srinagar
citation: Department of Microbiology, Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Soura, Srinagar. Antibiogram for the year 2023. Srinagar: SKIMS; 2024.
reporting: Percent susceptible by organism, specimen (blood; pus and body fluids; urine) and location (IPD, OPD, ICU), with n per location; organism isolation tables by specimen and location.
method: Testing according to CLSI M100, 33rd ed. (2023); species with test data for fewer than 30 isolates generally excluded (as stated).

verification.note: Six susceptibility tables (pages 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11) parsed from the PDF text layer by word position inside the ruled grid (pdfplumber), then every cell compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 2.3 to 2.6 and cropped into quarters (values in red cells read at high zoom); organism tables (pages 3, 6, 9) read from the text layer and checked on the images (2026-09-26). A blind re-read of 6 random cells (value read from a crop of header and row before looking at the extracted value) found no differences.

notes: Specimen-wise antibiogram with each organism split by IPD (wards), OPD and ICU. "Pus & body fluids" is recorded as pus, wounds and body fluids. Cells printed as "-", "IR" or left blank are left out; values printed as 0 are recorded as 0. Ticarcillin + clavulanate columns have no drug key and are left out. Enterococcus gentamicin in blood is printed with an unexplained asterisk (e.g. "29*") and recorded as gentamicin. Footnotes say all isolates were susceptible to colistin (blood, except Burkholderia) and to polymyxin B (pus and urine, except Proteus); these are not table values and are not recorded. Downloaded from the Wayback Machine snapshot web.archive.org/web/20250607132031id_/ of the URL (the SKIMS server refuses scripted downloads). The pus and body fluids S. aureus OPD row and the page 2 sample totals for pus and body fluids and for urine are identical to the 2022 report.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 741 cells of the six susceptibility tables (the seeded sample of 185 plus every other cell), all 63 row n with their IPD/OPD/ICU labels and all 114 organism-table counts re-read against the page images (scale 3 to 4.2, tables cropped into halves or bands; red cells read from the red channel so the dark digits stand out), each value read before comparing. 0 transcription errors in values, n, settings, organisms or counts; nothing corrected. The 38 ticarcillin-clavulanate cells are correctly left out.

Cells not kept by the rules, re-read and printed as recorded: Enterococcus gentamicin in blood (29* and 23*), pus and body fluids (55.6, 88.9, 0) and urine (56.9, 81.5, 0) and Pseudomonas pus ampicillin-sulbactam 15.4, 14.3 and 0 (intrinsic); cautions: blood Pseudomonas ICU ceftazidime 5, aztreonam 6, doripenem 5 (n=13); blood Salmonella IPD ceftriaxone 98 (n=30); blood Enterobacter IPD amikacin 65, gentamicin 52, ciprofloxacin 47, levofloxacin 65, tigecycline 46 (n=10); blood B. cepacia IPD meropenem 98 (n=12); pus S. aureus IPD cefoxitin 13.5 and erythromycin 20.6 and OPD 15.6 and 32.6; pus Proteus IPD aztreonam 38.9 (n=17); urine E. coli ICU imipenem 66.7 against meropenem 100; urine Proteus IPD cefotaxime 0 against ceftriaxone 50.

Count mismatch confirmed as printed: the pus and body fluids Gram-positive table heads S. aureus (n=294) but prints IPD (n=15) and OPD (n=14), while the organism table on page 6 gives 150 IPD, 141 OPD and 3 ICU (total 294). n kept as printed with the row notes. The OPD figures fit 141 isolates (15.6% = 22/141, 32.6% = 46/141) and all seven OPD values equal the 2022 report's OPD row (n=141), checked on the 2022 page 7: the row may be carried over from 2022.

Also confirmed: the page 2 sample totals for pus and body fluids and for urine repeat the 2022 report; the heading "Pus & body fluids" (filed as pus with that specimen_as_printed); the institution reads "Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Srinagar"; the Wayback copy of the PDF is complete (12 pages, ends with %%EOF).
